description: Versioned performance budgets (distributed-testing E4). scripts/compare-performance.py loads this file and applies its rule to scripts/performance.sh comparisons: a target-base comparison AND a comparison against the versioned fixed baseline (test/performance/baseline.json). Values are calibrated on ONE recorded runner (see calibration.runner); they are not portable. Q2 (isolated performance runners) is unresolved, so recalibrating on the promoted runner is a G6 promotion precondition. Every change to decision/families/slos/bundle/rerun_policy/fixed_baseline needs a new `changes` entry whose values_sha256 matches (enforced by the comparator and scripts/test_compare_performance.py).

decision.method: Per series: Hodges-Lehmann shift of log(candidate) over log(reference), i.e. a ratio, with a distribution-free one-sided Moses bound (normal approximation for the order-statistic index, rounded to the wider side). The degradation ratio is candidate/reference for lower-is-better series and reference/candidate for higher-is-better ones, so > 1 is always worse. One-sided Mann-Whitney p-values (tie and continuity corrected) test 'worse' and 'better'.
decision.non_inferiority: A series passes only when the one-sided upper bound of its degradation ratio is <= 1 + max_relative_degradation at alpha_non_inferiority / attempts_allowed (the level is split across the allowed attempts up front, so bounded reruns cannot shop for a pass). A run passes only when EVERY series is non-inferior: an intersection-union test, valid without a multiplicity correction.
decision.material_regression: A series is `slower` when its one-sided 'worse' p-value is significant after Holm within its family AND the Hodges-Lehmann degradation point estimate exceeds 1 + max_relative_degradation. A significant slowdown whose upper bound stays within the margin is `within_budget` (exit 0, reported).
decision.multiple_comparison: Holm step-down per family at alpha_family = alpha / (number of families with an informative series), for both the 'worse' and the 'better' direction. Holm is valid under arbitrary dependence, so no number of individually (uncorrected) significant series fails a family by itself; only a Holm-significant material regression does. The uncorrected count is still reported per family.
decision.correlated_series: Benchmarks in one sample share one `go test` process and its host state, and browser series share one Playwright run, so their false positives cluster (the W7-beta A/A moved six ns/op series by about 2% together). Holm is used because it does not assume independence, and the margins sit above the observed common-mode shift. A common-mode shift is visible as the family geomean_degradation; it never counts as independent evidence.
decision.aggregation: Series verdicts roll up by precedence fail > slower > slo_breach > inconclusive > within_budget > faster > no_significant_difference, per family, per comparison (target base, fixed baseline, SLOs), and overall. Family geometric-mean degradation is reported, not gated.
decision.inconclusive: A series is inconclusive when it is undersampled (n below min_samples, or too few samples to bound the shift), noisy (either side's CV above max_cv), or its upper bound exceeds the margin without a Holm-significant material regression. Mismatched provenance (platform, Go version, host, catalog, settings) makes the whole comparison inconclusive and not rerun-eligible.
decision.optimization_claims: `faster` requires a Holm-significant improvement with every other series non-inferior. The report's optimization_claim lists series that moved in the worse direction; a claim must name those tradeoffs. Neutral performance (no_significant_difference) is a valid result.
decision.correctness_first: Correctness, completion, provenance, instrumented images and benchmark harness identity fail closed (exit 2) before any speed comparison, exactly as in E3.

absolute_budgets.enforced_by: ui/scripts/check-bundle-size.mjs (these values must stay in lockstep with its defaults; a unit test asserts it)

bundle.rationale: Bundle sizes are deterministic (identical across all A/A sides), so there is no noise to calibrate. The absolute ceilings are check-bundle-size.mjs's (enforced there and as SLOs here). The relative bounds are review thresholds: one change may grow a size by at most 5% of its base, and the cumulative growth against the fixed baseline is capped at 10% before the baseline must be re-recorded with a reviewed budgets change.

rerun_policy.rerun_on: inconclusive only; fail, slower and slo_breach are terminal and are never rerun
not_rerun_eligible: provenance mismatch between base and candidate
fixed baseline missing, unreadable, from a different runner/setup, or lacking a series
between_attempts: fresh artifacts directory and fresh server/benchmark processes
server phases start with the other side (candidate first on even attempts)
images, harness, settings and repeats are unchanged; the attempt's alpha_non_inferiority share is fixed in advance
rerun_policy.pooling: none: every attempt is judged on its own samples; every attempt's report is retained
rerun_policy.unresolved: an inconclusive last attempt (or a non-rerunnable inconclusive) becomes `inconclusive_unresolved`, exit 3; the strict gate must block

fixed_baseline.rationale: The fixed baseline is not interleaved with the candidate, so it is only meaningful on the recorded runner and setup. Anything else is inconclusive, never silently compared. Its margins (fixed_baseline_max_relative_degradation) are calibrated from cross-run drift between separate A/A runs, which is larger than within-run noise.

limitations: Q2 is unresolved: there is no isolated performance runner. These values are calibrated on the runner above only. The fixed baseline and every budget refuse (inconclusive) or mean nothing on another host_id/platform; recalibrating on the promoted runner (new A/A runs, a new baseline, a reviewed budgets change) is a G6 promotion precondition.

Three full A/A runs and one load-only open-workload A/A run are a small calibration set. Margins use the worst observed per-side noise (including a run the stream's own host-side unit tests overlapped) to stay conservative; more A/A runs on an isolated runner should tighten the benchmark margins, which are wide for micro benchmarks (10-20%).
The host is a shared macOS workstation (Docker Desktop VM, persistent co-tenant containers, desktop processes). Host-level contention outside Docker is not controlled.
No performance lane exists in CI yet; nothing here gates a merge until G6 promotes it.
calibration.method: Same-code A/A control runs (CAESIUM_PERF_BASE_SHA = candidate SHA: one release image measured on both sides, interleaved exactly like an A/B run) through the unchanged E3 harness, evaluated with `scripts/compare-performance.py --calibrate`. Per series the worst per-side log-scale SD sets the margin (see each family's `derivation`); the cross-run pairs (every A/A run's candidate side against every other run's, i.e. non-interleaved, hours apart) set the fixed-baseline margins. The resulting rule is then re-applied to every A/A run: the tolerance is an A/A false-fail rate of 0 (and <= alpha by construction) and an A/A inconclusive rate <= 1 in 3 per attempt, so that an unchanged candidate is unresolved after three attempts with probability < 4%.

parameters.alpha: 0.05 family-wise per comparison (Holm per family at 0.05 / families tested); unchanged from E3's per-series alpha, now corrected.
parameters.alpha_non_inferiority: 0.05 split across the 3 allowed attempts (0.0167 per attempt, z = 2.13).
parameters.min_samples: 10 per side for every series: the largest per-series minimum implied by the calibrated margins is at most 10, and the SLOs need 10 samples for a nearest-rank p90 that excludes exactly one stalled sample.
parameters.max_reruns: 2 (3 attempts). With the observed A/A per-attempt inconclusive rate, an unchanged candidate resolves within 3 attempts with probability > 96%; more attempts would dilute the non-inferiority alpha further.
parameters.max_cv: per series, max(0.10, 2 x the largest A/A CV), rounded up to 5%: flags contended runs (the W7-beta contended A/B had benchmark CVs 0.15-0.33) as noisy instead of comparing them.

changes.rationale: Budget open-api-read-mix (#588, distributed-testing H2). Its warm-server sustained failure was a product defect, not a workload expectation error: the embedded dqlite node left Nagle's algorithm on for the connections it accepts, so every query whose result spanned more than one 4 KiB response part waited for the client's delayed ACK (~40 ms per stall). Run reads cost ~86 ms instead of ~1.4 ms, run lists crossed the threshold once a job held about five runs, and under the 10 reads/s mix the read pool and the single write connection queued behind those stalls until completions fell behind arrivals. pkg/db now sets TCP_NODELAY on the node's listener and accepted sockets. With the fix the catalog rate and read mix are unchanged and sustained on a warm server, so this entry adds duration rules and cold/warm sustained, warm throughput, warm latency and warm read-latency SLOs for it, derived with the version 1 method. It also gives the read mix an explicit error and drop policy that fails closed: per-sample read error ratio (non-2xx, transport failures and drops over offered) at most 1%, dropped reads at most 2 and successful reads at least 100, cold and warm (added in review of #594). No existing value changes.
changes.evidence: budgets.calibration: A/A perf-w9g-aa1 (fixed build, load only, open-tiny-sustained + open-api-read-mix, 10 repeats) calibrated the values; out-of-sample A/A perf-w9g-aa2 and perf-w9g-aa3 (aa3 run by the corrected harness and judged in-run by these budgets) confirm them (calibration.open_workload_results.post_fix). The reproduction, bisection and regression-test evidence is in the H2 note of docs/exec-plans/active/distributed-testing.md.
